categories.main_business_segments: Halliburton operates two primary business segments: Completion and Production, which delivers cementing, stimulation, intervention, pressure control, artificial lift, and completion products and services; and Drilling and Evaluation, which provides field and reservoir modeling, drilling, fluids and specialty chemicals, evaluation and wellbore placement solutions. The company serves major, national, and independent oil and natural gas companies worldwide with a comprehensive range of oilfield services and products.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company's core technologies include hydraulic fracturing systems, directional drilling and measurement-while-drilling services, wireline and perforating services, drilling fluid systems, completion tools and intelligent well completions, artificial lift solutions including electrical submersible pumps, and cloud-based digital services with artificial intelligence for subsurface insights. Manufacturing capabilities include in-house production of most equipment, providing flexibility to adjust capital expenditures based on market conditions.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Halliburton serves major, national, and independent oil and natural gas companies engaged in exploration, development, and production activities. The company operates across upstream, midstream, and downstream sectors, with no single customer representing more than 10% of consolidated revenue. Primary end markets include onshore and offshore oil and gas drilling, well completion, production optimization, and pipeline services globally.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates in more than 70 countries across four primary geographic regions: North America (45% of 2022 revenue), Latin America (16%), Europe/Africa/CIS (13%), and Middle East/Asia (24%). The United States accounted for 45% of consolidated revenue in 2022. Major facilities are located in the United States, United Kingdom, Malaysia, Saudi Arabia, and other key energy markets worldwide.
categories.supply_chain_position: Halliburton operates across the entire oilfield services value chain, from upstream exploration and drilling services through well completion and production optimization. The company is positioned in the midstream and downstream segments through its drilling fluids, completion tools, and production enhancement services. It manufactures most of its own equipment and manages procurement of raw materials including proppants, chemicals, metals, and gels.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include accelerating digital and automation technology deployment for technical differentiation and operational efficiency, maintaining capital expenditures at 5-6% of revenue while focusing on technological advancements, expanding international growth in onshore and offshore markets, and developing solutions for the energy mix transition including carbon capture and storage, hydrogen, and geothermal projects. The company targets a 40% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2035 from 2018 baseline and operates Halliburton Labs, a clean energy accelerator with 21 participating companies.
categories.revenue_model: Halliburton generates revenue primarily through service delivery and product sales to oil and gas companies. Services are typically priced on a per-day, per-meter, per-man-hour, or similar basis with short-term contracts. The company also provides software and integrated project management services on longer-term contracts. In 2022, services represented 73% of total revenue ($14.7 billion) and product sales represented 27% ($5.5 billion).
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Halliburton is one of the world's largest diversified energy services companies operating in highly competitive markets with many substantial competitors. The company competes on price, service delivery, health and safety standards, service quality, global talent retention, geological expertise, product quality, warranty, and technical proficiency. Competitive factors and the vast geographic scope make it impractical to estimate total competitors, but the company maintains significant market presence across all service lines.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: Halliburton is a large-cap company with approximately $20.3 billion in total revenue for 2022, representing 33% growth from $15.3 billion in 2021. The company generated $2.7 billion in operating income in 2022 compared to $1.8 billion in 2021, with operating margins of 18% for Completion and Production and 15% for Drilling and Evaluation. The company has approximately 45,000 employees representing 130 nationalities and generated $2.2 billion in operating cash flow in 2022.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Halliburton's value proposition centers on collaborating and engineering solutions to maximize asset value for customers while improving efficiency, increasing recovery, and maximizing production. Key differentiators include over 100 years of operational experience, advanced digital and automation technologies, proprietary hydraulic fracturing fluid systems including food-industry-sourced materials, low-emissions equipment, intelligent field management solutions, and integrated project management capabilities. The company emphasizes technical proficiency, innovation, and customer-focused service delivery across the complete reservoir lifecycle.
